newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank again supports crown through fixing.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank again supports crown through fixing.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Wednesday again supported the crown by fixing it stronger against the market and dealers said the move could bring a longer-term strengthening trend for the currency.
The NBS fixed the crown at 33.169 to the dollar and at 19.643 to the mark, implying a deviation against the crown's mark/dollar basket parity of -0.78 percent.
At the time of the fixing calculation the crown was trading at -1.09 percent versus its midpoint.
"This stronger fixing will definitely reverse the crown's weakening trend and the currency will now strengthen," said Peter Koprna, a chief dealer at Slovenska Sporitelna.

Koprna said he expected the first resistance for an uptrend at around -0.70 percent versus the basket, but added the currency had the potential to move to around 25 basis points on the depreciation side of parity.
The crown weakened sharply on Wednesday morning in a round of speculative selling started by local banks. But foreign purchases of cheap crowns helped the currency firm slightly soon after.

The crown touched levels of 170 basis points on the depreciation side shortly after Wednesday's open, but it then firmed to around -1.30 percent against midpoint and hovered slightly below -1.00 percent until the NBS fixing.

"Today's fixing was a clear signal that the central bank does not want to see the crown weaker, but the question is how long it will be enough to intervene only through fixing," said one Bratislava-based dealer from a foreign bank.

"So far the pressure on the crown was not as strong as on its Czech counterpart, so it was not necessary for the NBS to add foreign currencies to domestic banks elsewhere than at its fixing, but nobody can say where the crown will go if foreign pressure intensifies," he added.
